answer: A terrace sponsorship gate stops bulk fakes draining a reward pool. A newcomer needs a sponsor locking 25 units each on a four-seat terrace with a cipher seal bound to it; falcon auditors sample identities, and one fake sends a signal forfeiting its collateral and halving its quota. The k-th fake costs 42 plus 2 per earlier group, so cost rises with n, collateral is non-reusable, and failure loses the stake. One fake costs 42, and 1,000 cost 291,000 units. A guarantor collusion ring fails when one fake wipes its terrace. Honest agents pay once, keeping rewards.
